WizardSubtitle: Adjust gamma and gray balance, compare the result, then save a Windows calibration profile.
StepInstruction0: Let the display warm up. Choose its normal color mode and native resolution. Turn off HDR and Night light while calibrating. Start calibration to preview adjustments on the selected display.
StepInstruction1: At your usual viewing distance, adjust gamma until the center dots blend into the surrounding checkerboard.
StepInstruction2: Note your monitor's brightness setting. Adjust it until you can just see the darker patches on the left against the black background. You can skip brightness and contrast if your monitor lacks these controls.
StepInstruction3: Note your monitor's contrast setting. Adjust it to keep the pale patches on the right distinguishable from the white background. If you cancel, restore the brightness and contrast on the monitor.
StepInstruction4: Adjust red, green and blue until the gray patches look neutral. Lower a channel to remove its color cast. Gains above 1 may clip highlights. Reset returns to the neutral parameters captured at the beginning.
StepInstruction5: Compare the original and adjusted curves, then name and save the result. The same countdown continues as you switch views. If it expires, the app restores the original curve.
